title: Void Ending in an Opposition to Pluto
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The opposition is the hardest figure the Moon can close on: the text grades it as extreme enmity, because the signs it joins stand opposed across all four natural qualities. It shares with the square the warnings that guard every election, and a Moon waning in light and faced by Saturn is the source's own example of a serious misfortune.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with an opposition to Pluto, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his buried endings. Pluto is unknown to Picatrix, found in 1930 and outside the world the book describes at every point. Any reading of it here is this almanac's extension of Picatrix's doctrine, never the source's own words. Named for the Roman lord of the underworld, it is read as the far, dark hinge of the set: a course that closes on it ends in the buried kind of ending, the small death of a matter before the next sign begins.
